summary: Tabasco is one of six state legislatures (with Aguascalientes, Chiapas, Durango, Querétaro and Tamaulipas) that have enacted no legal gender-recognition procedure at all — Human Rights Watch, March 2025, against a national tally of 22 of 32 states having legislated one. HRW's dedicated March 2024 report on the state, co-produced with a local inclusion centre, documented that the absence keeps trans people's identity documents permanently mismatched and exposes them to police and institutional mistreatment — document mismatch being the practical trigger for police questioning of a visible visitor. A widely circulated January 2023 claim that Tabasco added a criminal 'anti-eccentricity' provision failed the dossier's three-source verification and is not treated as a finding.

The Guardian (24 July 2024): Mexico City's legislature approved the 'Paola Buenrostro law' making transfeminicide a distinct criminal offence, named for a trans woman murdered in 2016 whose killing remains unpunished; the report covers the vote and celebrants outside the congress building.

localsOnly: The recognition vacuum binds residents hardest in daily institutional life — identity papers, services and detention treatment — per the HRW 2024 report's documentation.
